video.title: 5 Boring Side Hustles That ALWAYS Work (90% Success Rate)

summary: Casper Capital presents five broad categories of boring side hustles: resale, tutoring, local services, rentals and vending or ATMs. The narrator gives beginner steps and several hypothetical earnings examples, then offers a framework based on recurring, durable demand. Most ideas involve physical work, so they would need substantial human involvement to run.

ideas.name: Reselling used items
ideas.one_liner: Buy or source used goods, then resell them through online marketplaces or live shopping platforms.
ideas.business_model: Buy low and resell at a higher price; per-item sales.
ideas.customer: People looking for a good deal, including buyers of collectibles, sneakers and vintage items.
ideas.problem: Buyers want affordable goods and the feeling of getting a bargain.
ideas.offer: Used furniture and other secondhand items, listed on marketplaces or sold in live auctions.

pricing.model: Per-item resale; specific sale prices are not stated.
pricing.notes: Profit figures are hypothetical and not tied to a stated item price.

acquisition_channels.details: List household items on Facebook Marketplace or eBay, then experiment with Poshmark, Mercari, TikTok Shop or Whatnot.

quote.text: list extra stuff around your house on platforms like Facebook Marketplace or eBay.
quote.speaker: Unknown narrator

acquisition_channels.details: Whatnot is described as live shopping, particularly for collectibles, sneakers and vintage items.

quote.text: It's huge for collectibles, sneakers, vintage items, and it's more like a live auction rather than a Facebook marketplace listing.
quote.speaker: Unknown narrator

ideas.delivery: Source items, repair or fix some furniture, photograph and list items, then arrange delivery or handover. The seller does the sourcing, repairs and delivery.
unit_economics_claims: The narrator says reselling 10 to 20 times a month could produce a couple thousand dollars in monthly profit.
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated; the narrator suggests starting with items already at home.

acquisition.how: Agents could draft listings and answer routine buyer questions, but sourcing goods and creating accurate listings need human checks.

onboarding.how: Marketplace checkout can handle routine purchases; custom collection or delivery arrangements may need a person.

delivery.how: Sourcing, fixing and delivering physical items require human work.

billing.how: Marketplace payment flows can automate routine payment collection, with occasional dispute handling.

support.how: Agents could handle basic questions, but item condition, returns and delivery problems need human judgment.

uk_applicability.notes: Secondhand resale and marketplace listings work in the UK; platform availability and local demand can vary.

risks: Items may take time to sell, tying up cash and storage space.
Sourcing, repairs and delivery take time.
Condition disputes and unsafe or unreliable handovers can create problems.
